# Flyology Runtime

> Flyology Runtime is an experimental GNAT runtime extension for ordinary Ada tasking. It combines interoperable native and lightweight execution lanes with task-aware I/O while preserving ordinary Ada task semantics and synchronous control flow.

Flyology uses the terms "lightweight task" and "native task." Lightweight scheduling is cooperative, not preemptive. The project does not claim production qualification, universal portability, or hard real-time behavior. Runtime preparation supports only the exact host and compiler release pairs documented by the project; do not infer support from the broader Alire dependency range.

## Documentation

- [Overview](https://flyology.org/): Project scope, programming model, included building blocks, and important constraints.
- [Guide](https://flyology.org/guide/): Toolchain requirements, runtime preparation, task designation, stack and memory policy, execution groups, task-aware I/O, resource budgets, observability, verification, and constraints.
- [Architecture](https://flyology.org/architecture/): Tasking integration, native and lightweight lanes, schedulers, pollers, stackful contexts, memory ownership, and lifecycle boundaries.
- [Timers and clock changes](https://flyology.org/guide/timers/): Relative, monotonic, bounded multi-deadline, and wall-clock timer behavior, including complete due activation batches and backward clock changes.
- [HTTP applications](https://flyology.org/guide/http/): Optional HTTP routing, middleware, streaming, structured request work, WebSockets, security, and measurement guidance.
- [API reference](https://flyology.org/api/): Generated reference for Flyology's public Ada packages.

## Project sources

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flyology-ada/flyology/main/README.md): Detailed user-facing architecture, configuration, APIs, examples, constraints, and verification commands.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/flyology-ada/flyology): Ada sources, runtime integration, tests, proof model, scripts, showcases, and website sources.
- [Supported runtime patch matrix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flyology-ada/flyology/main/runtime/patches/README.md): Exact verified host, compiler, and GNAT runtime patch families.
- [Alire crate manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flyology-ada/flyology/main/alire.toml): Package metadata and dependency constraints; these constraints are broader than the verified runtime matrix.

## Optional

- [WebSocket conformance reports](https://flyology.org/reports/websocket/): Dated Autobahn framing, compression, limits, TLS, and timing results with per-profile details.
- [Development journal](https://flyology.org/journal/): Dated implementation notes, measurements, corrections, and operating boundaries.
- [Flyology Postgres](https://postgres.flyology.org/): A separate ecosystem project exploring PostgreSQL access with Flyology.
